title: Quantum Simulation Of Nuclear Dynamics In First Quantization
authors: Luca Spagnoli, Chiara Lissoni, And Alessandro Roggero
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2200 (2026).

The study of real time dynamics of nuclear systems is of great importance to provide theoretical predictions of cross sections relevant for both terrestrial experiments as well as applications in astrophysics. First principles simulations of these dynamical processes is however hindered by an exponential cost in classical resources and the possibility of performing scalable simulations using quantum computers is currently an active field of research. In this work we provide the first complete characterization of the resource requirements for studying nuclear dynamics with the full Leading Order (LO) pionless EFT Hamiltonian in first quantization employing simulation strategies using both product formulas as well as Quantum Signal Processing. In particular, we show that time evolution of such an Hamiltonian can be performed with polynomial resources in the number of particles, and logarithmic resources in the number of single-particle basis states. This result provides an exponential improvement compared with previous work on the same Hamiltonian model in second quantization. We find that interesting simulations for low energy nuclear scattering could be achievable with tens of millions of T gates and few hundred logical qubits suggesting that the study of simple nuclear reactions could be amenable for early fault tolerant quantum platforms.

.
tldr: Characterizes resource requirements for quantum simulation of nuclear dynamics using first quantization with the leading-order pionless EFT Hamiltonian, showing polynomial scaling in particle number and logarithmic scaling in basis size.
motivation: Real-time simulations of nuclear systems are classically intractable due to exponential resource costs, motivating the use of quantum computers for scalable predictions of scattering cross sections.
method: Employs product formulas and quantum signal processing to simulate time evolution under the LO pionless EFT Hamiltonian in first quantization, with detailed resource estimation for T gates and logical qubits.
result: Demonstrates polynomial scaling in the number of particles and logarithmic scaling in single-particle basis states, yielding an exponential improvement over prior second-quantization approaches; low-energy nuclear scattering may require tens of millions of T gates and a few hundred logical qubits.
conclusion: Simple nuclear reactions could be within reach of early fault-tolerant quantum platforms, though the work is an application of quantum simulation rather than a contribution to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: On The Relation Between Perspective-neutral, Algebraic, And Effective Quantum Reference Frames
authors: Julian de Vuyst, Philipp A. Hoehn, And Artur Tsobanjan
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2196 (2026).

The framework of internal quantum reference frames (QRFs) constitutes a universal toolset for dealing with symmetries in quantum theory and has led to new revelations in quantum gravity, gauge theories and foundational physics. Multiple approaches have emerged, sometimes differing in scope and the way symmetries are implemented, raising the question as to their relation. Here, we investigate the relation between three approaches to QRFs for gauge symmetries, namely the [MATH] semiclassical, [MATH], and [MATH] (PN) approaches. Rather than constructing Hilbert spaces, as the PN approach, the effective approach is based on a quantum phase space parametrized by expectation values and fluctuations, while the emphasis of the algebraic approach is on the state space of complex linear functionals on a kinematical algebra. Nevertheless, external frame information is treated as gauge in all three formalisms, manifested in constraints on states and algebra. We show that these three approaches are, in fact, equivalent for ideal QRFs, distinguished by sharp orientations, which is the previous setting of the first two approaches. Our demonstration pertains to single constraints, including relativistic ones, and encompasses QRF changes. In particular, the QRF transformations of the PN framework agree semiclassically with those of the older effective approach, by which it was inspired. As a physical application, we explore the QRF covariance of uncertainties and fluctuations, which turn out to be frame dependent. This is particularly well-suited for the effective and algebraic approaches, for which these quantities form a natural basis. Finally, we pave the way towards extending these two approaches to non-ideal QRFs by studying the projection and gauge-fixing operations of the Page-Wootters formalism, built into the PN framework, on algebraic states.

.
tldr: The paper shows that three approaches to quantum reference frames—perspective-neutral, algebraic, and effective—are equivalent for ideal reference frames with sharp orientations, and examines the frame dependence of uncertainties.
motivation: Multiple frameworks for internal quantum reference frames have emerged with different scopes and symmetry implementations, raising the question of how they relate to one another.
method: The authors compare the perspective-neutral Hilbert-space approach, the algebraic approach based on states on a kinematical algebra, and the effective quantum phase-space approach, demonstrating equivalence for ideal QRFs and connecting QRF transformations, including via Page-Wootters projection and gauge-fixing.
result: The three formalisms are equivalent for ideal QRFs; the perspective-neutral QRF transformations agree semiclassically with the effective approach, and uncertainties/fluctuations are shown to be frame dependent.
conclusion: The work unifies several QRF formalisms and paves the way for extending the effective and algebraic approaches to non-ideal QRFs.

title: Quantum Phase Estimation With Optimal Confidence Interval Using Three Control Qubits
authors: Kaur Kristjuhan And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2193 (2026).

Quantum phase estimation is an important routine in many quantum algorithms, particularly for estimating the ground state energy in quantum chemistry simulations. This estimation involves applying powers of a unitary to the ground state, controlled by an auxiliary state prepared on a control register. In many applications the goal is to provide a confidence interval for the phase estimate, and optimal performance is provided by a discrete prolate spheroidal sequence. We show how to prepare the corresponding state in a far more efficient way than prior work. We find that a matrix product state representation with a bond dimension of 4 is sufficient to give a highly accurate approximation for all dimensions tested, up to [MATH]. This matrix product state can be efficiently prepared using a sequence of simple three-qubit operations. When the dimension is a power of 2, the phase estimation can be performed with only three qubits for the control register, making it suitable for early-generation fault-tolerant quantum computers with a limited number of logical qubits.

﻿

.
tldr: The paper presents an efficient matrix product state method to prepare optimal control states for quantum phase estimation using only three control qubits, enabling accurate confidence intervals on early fault-tolerant quantum computers.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is crucial for ground-state energy estimation in quantum chemistry, but achieving optimal confidence intervals requires preparing discrete prolate spheroidal sequence states, which are difficult to implement efficiently.
method: They represent the optimal control state as a matrix product state with bond dimension 4 and prepare it using a sequence of simple three-qubit operations, showing high accuracy for dimensions up to a large power of 2.
result: The MPS approximation is highly accurate for all tested dimensions, and when the dimension is a power of 2, phase estimation can be performed with only three control qubits.
conclusion: This approach makes optimal-confidence quantum phase estimation feasible on early fault-tolerant quantum computers with a limited number of logical qubits.

title: Hybrid Vqe-cvqe Algorithm Using Diabatic State Preparation
authors: C Stephen Hellberg And Daniel Gunlycke John P T Stenger
abstract: We propose a hybrid variational quantum algorithm that has variational parameters used by both the quantum circuit and the subsequent classical optimization. Similar to the variational quantum eigensolver, this algorithm applies a parameterized unitary operator to the qubit register. We generate this operator using diabatic state preparation. The quantum measurement results then inform the classical optimization procedure used by the cascaded variational quantum eigensolver. We demonstrate the algorithm on a system of interacting electrons and show how it can be used on long-term error-corrected as well as short-term intermediate-scale quantum computers. Our simulations performed on IBM Brisbane produced energies well within chemical accuracy.
tldr: The paper proposes a hybrid VQE-CVQE variational quantum algorithm that uses diabatic state preparation to generate a parameterized unitary for quantum chemistry simulations.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms are promising for near-term quantum devices and fault-tolerant quantum computers, but require efficient state preparation and optimization strategies.
method: The algorithm applies a parameterized unitary operator generated by diabatic state preparation to a qubit register, uses measurement results to inform a classical cascaded variational quantum eigensolver optimization, and is demonstrated on a system of interacting electrons via simulations on IBM Brisbane.
result: The simulations produced energies well within chemical accuracy for the interacting electron system.
conclusion: The hybrid VQE-CVQE algorithm is applicable to both long-term error-corrected and short-term intermediate-scale quantum computers for quantum chemistry problems.

title: Observation Of Even-denominator Fractional Quantum Hall States At Ν = 3/4 And 5/4 In The Lowest Landau Level
authors: Siddharth Kumar Singh, Chengyu Wang, Adbhut Gupta, Kirk W Baldwin, Loren N Pfeiffer And Mansour Shayegan
abstract: Two-dimensional electron systems (2DESs) confined to wide GaAs quantum wells (QWs) provide a unique platform to study exotic fractional quantum Hall states (FQHSs) because the 2DES has a bilayer charge distribution with significant interlayer tunneling. Precise control over the 2DES density allows the tuning of the interlayer tunneling over a wide range. Here, we present our discovery of new even-denominator FQHSs in the lowest Landau level (orbital index N = 0) at filling factors and 5/4 in an ultrahigh-quality 2DES confined to a 72.5 nm-wide GaAs QW. The ground states at and 5/4 both evolve from composite fermion (CF) Fermi seas to FQHSs as the density is raised so that interlayer tunneling is sufficiently reduced and the 2DES becomes two-component, signaled by the behavior of the FQHSs flanking and 5/4. The two-component nature of the and 5/4 FQHSs is also evident from their extreme sensitivity to the bilayer charge distribution symmetry: both states disappear quickly when the charge distribution is made asymmetric by only . We find a natural explanation for the 3/4 and 5/4 FQHSs in terms of two states linked by particle-hole symmetry, and using Scarola-Jain bilayer CF framework which is a generalization of the well-known, two-component, Halperin state ( state). Our observations elucidate the crucial role of competing energy and length scales in wide QW in stabilizing new ground states.
tldr: Observation of new even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states at filling factors 3/4 and 5/4 in the lowest Landau level of a wide GaAs quantum well.
motivation: Wide GaAs quantum wells provide a tunable platform for studying exotic fractional quantum Hall states due to bilayer charge distribution and interlayer tunneling.
method: Transport measurements on ultrahigh-quality two-dimensional electron systems confined to a 72.5 nm-wide GaAs quantum well, tuning density and charge distribution symmetry.
result: Two new even-denominator FQHSs at 3/4 and 5/4 emerge from composite fermion Fermi seas as interlayer tunneling is reduced; both are extremely sensitive to charge distribution asymmetry.
conclusion: The 3/4 and 5/4 states are naturally explained by particle-hole symmetry and the Scarola-Jain bilayer composite fermion framework, highlighting competing energy and length scales in wide quantum wells.

title: Pressure-induced Ising Superconductivity In Organic-intercalated 1T-TaS2
authors: Jiaqi Chen, Shuyang Wang, Lixuan Yu, Xuliang Chen, Chao An, Yonghui Zhou, Yilin Wang And Zhaorong Yang
abstract: Layered transition metal dichalcogenides host a rich landscape of correlated electronic phases that are profoundly sensitive to interlayer coupling. Although both thinning and pressure have been individually used to tune these properties, the high-pressure behavior of low-dimensional systems remains largely unexplored. Here, we propose a synergistic tuning strategy by combination of organic cation intercalation and pressure to simulate the properties of low-dimensional materials under pressure. We show that intercalating cetyltrimethylammonium cations into the bulk 1T-TaS2 significantly weakens the interlayer coupling and leads to an effective reduction in dimensionality. Moreover, the intercalated sample exhibits distinct features under high pressure as compared with non-intercalated one. The superconductivity in the intercalated sample is induced accompanied by a complete suppression of nearly commensurate charge density wave order, differing from the melting of commensurate state in the non-intercalated case. Upon further compression up to 58.1 GPa, the superconductivity displays a dome-shaped evolution, also without showing re-enhancement that presented in the non-intercalated sample. More strikingly, the superconductivity in the intercalated 1T-TaS2 displays signatures of Ising superconductivity, with its in-plane upper critical field exceeding twice the Pauli paramagnetic limit. Our findings not only provide a powerful route for tuning the collective electronic states but also open up possibilities in searching for emergent phenomena in low-dimensional materials.
tldr: Organic cation intercalation combined with high pressure tunes interlayer coupling in 1T-TaS2, inducing Ising superconductivity with an in-plane upper critical field exceeding twice the Pauli limit.
motivation: Low-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenides host correlated electronic phases highly sensitive to interlayer coupling, but the high-pressure behavior of such low-dimensional systems is largely unexplored.
method: Cetyltrimethylammonium cations were intercalated into bulk 1T-TaS2 to weaken interlayer coupling and effectively reduce dimensionality, followed by high-pressure transport measurements up to 58.1 GPa.
result: Superconductivity emerges alongside complete suppression of the nearly commensurate charge density wave order, follows a dome-shaped evolution with pressure, and shows Ising superconductivity signatures with in-plane upper critical field above twice the Pauli paramagnetic limit.
conclusion: The intercalation-plus-pressure strategy offers a powerful route to tune collective electronic states and search for emergent phenomena in low-dimensional materials.

title: Altermagnetism And Superconductivity: A Short Historical Review
authors: Hui Hu And Xia-Ji Liu Zhao Liu
abstract: This review is organized into three parts. In the first part, we explore the deep interconnections among three seemingly unrelated concepts in condensed matter physics: electronic liquid crystal (ELC) phases, multipole expansions, and altermagnetism (AM). At the heart of these phenomena lies a shared foundation: spin-momentum locking in the nonrelativistic regime. Originally proposed in the context of ELC phases, nonrelativistic spin-momentum locking (NRSML) was later elegantly incorporated into the formalism of multipole expansions. This framework can be further extended across multiple atomic sites, making it particularly effective for describing AMs, which host localized magnetic moments with anisotropic magnetization densities distributed over sublattices. In the second part, we examine superconducting (SC) phenomena associated with AM from three complementary perspectives. First, we investigate SC associated with NRSML Fermi surfaces (FSs), the unifying theme of the first part, highlighting a rich variety of unconventional SC states. These include finite-momentum pairing, -wave and spin-triplet SC, and topological Bogoliubov FSs, among others. We then review SC emerging from either static AM order or AM fluctuations. Finally, we discuss the possible competition and intertwining between AM order and SC, illustrated using the repulsive Hubbard model. Additional related topics are addressed in the concluding part. Overall, this work offers both an accessible introduction to the newly identified magnetic order known as AM and a conceptual guide for researchers aiming to harness the ensuing unconventional SC in the development of future quantum technologies.
tldr: A historical review linking electronic liquid crystal phases, multipole expansions, and altermagnetism via nonrelativistic spin-momentum locking, with implications for unconventional superconductivity.
motivation: To provide an accessible introduction to altermagnetism and a conceptual guide for harnessing its associated unconventional superconductivity in future quantum technologies.
method: Reviews theoretical frameworks connecting electronic liquid crystal phases, multipole expansions, and altermagnetism, then surveys superconducting phenomena arising from nonrelativistic spin-momentum locking Fermi surfaces, static altermagnetic order, and altermagnetic fluctuations.
result: Identifies a rich variety of unconventional superconducting states, including finite-momentum pairing, d-wave and spin-triplet superconductivity, and topological Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces, and discusses competition and intertwining between altermagnetic order and superconductivity in the repulsive Hubbard model.
conclusion: Altermagnetism offers a unifying perspective on spin-momentum locking and unconventional superconductivity, but the work remains a condensed-matter review without direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Symmetry-free Quantum-dot Metasurfaces Realize Arbitrary Polarization-direction Emission
authors: Jiazheng Qin, Zhou Zhou, Jianfeng Chen, Zhe Wang, Xinyu Wang, Zhaogang Dong, Yan Liu, Li Jun Lim, Jiangang Feng, Weijin Chen, Jin Hong Ng, Chang Hoong Chow, Victor Leong, Shuihua Yang, Xuan Dong, Yuzhi Shi, Zhi-Kuang Tan And Cheng-Wei Qiu
abstract: Emission from quantum dots (QDs) is inherently broadband, isotropic, and unpolarized, exhibiting poor spatial and temporal coherence that largely limits their applications in directional and polarization-controlled light sources. While resonant metasurfaces supporting symmetry-protected BICs can enhance emission through high-Q radiative resonances near the BIC in momentum space, their rigid symmetries confine emission to fixed directions and polarization states, preventing robust emission control. Here, we overcome the symmetry-imposed limitations by introducing a symmetry-free resonant metasurface that transforms incoherent QD emission into multiple directional illuminations with designable polarizations and enhanced spatial and temporal coherence. Our recipe allows continuous and robust control of emission while preserving resonance quality. Our approach unifies coherence enhancement and emission shaping within a unified framework, establishing a scalable and versatile platform for active photonic chips and tunable quantum light sources.
tldr: A symmetry-free quantum-dot metasurface enables arbitrary polarization-direction emission with enhanced spatial and temporal coherence.
motivation: Quantum dot emission is inherently broadband, isotropic, and unpolarized, which limits directional and polarization-controlled light sources. Existing symmetry-protected BIC metasurfaces restrict emission to fixed directions and polarizations.
method: The authors design a symmetry-free resonant metasurface that transforms incoherent quantum dot emission into multiple directional illuminations with designable polarizations, preserving resonance quality.
result: The approach achieves continuous and robust control of emission direction and polarization while enhancing spatial and temporal coherence, unifying coherence enhancement and emission shaping.
conclusion: The platform offers a scalable and versatile route for active photonic chips and tunable quantum light sources.

title: Intrinsic Phase-locking Of Terahertz Auto-oscillations In The Easy-plane Antiferromagnet Mn2Au
authors: Yiyue Wang, Wenbo Zhang, Hao-Hsuan Chen, Milad Jalali, Andrea Meo And Yaowen Liu
abstract: Antiferromagnets offer a promising platform for ultrafast spintronic emitters owing to their intrinsic terahertz ( ) spin dynamics, yet the mechanisms governing the onset and coherence of current-driven oscillations remain poorly understood. Here we develop a multiscale theoretical framework for the collinear antiferromagnet Mn2Au driven by a perpendicularly polarized spin current. Using a momentum-dependent canonical transformation of the coupled macrospin Hamiltonian, we show that the emergence of auto-oscillations is governed by a saddle-node bifurcation set by the in-plane fourfold anisotropy barrier. Moreover, we identify an intrinsic phase-locking mechanism that is threshold-free: once auto-oscillations are initiated, the interplay between easy-plane anisotropy and strong antiferromagnetic (AFM) exchange generates a robust restoring force that stabilizes the relative phase of the two sublattices throughout the simulated limit cycle. This behavior contrasts sharply with that of antiferromagnets with perpendicular anisotropy, where phase unlocking can destabilize the dynamics. Zero-temperature atomistic spin-dynamics (ASDs) simulations support the collective phase-locking picture in the full lattice model, and three independent K atomistic ASD spot checks show bounded thermal fluctuations, no phase slips, and a persistent spectral peak near THz. Stochastic two-sublattice collective-mode tests over – further indicate milliradian-scale relative-phase noise and show that a Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction-like perturbation mainly produces a static relative-phase offset rather than unlocking. Our results support Mn2Au as a highly coherent platform for continuous-wave generation and provide general design principles for stable AFM oscillators. Here, threshold-free refers to the absence of an additional microscopic relative-phase-locking threshold; the macroscopic onset of auto-oscillation remains finite and is set by the in-plane fourfold anisotropy barrier.
tldr: A theoretical study of intrinsic phase-locking in terahertz auto-oscillations of the easy-plane antiferromagnet Mn2Au driven by spin current.
motivation: Antiferromagnets are promising for ultrafast terahertz spintronic emitters, but the mechanisms governing the onset and coherence of current-driven oscillations are poorly understood.
method: The authors develop a multiscale framework using a momentum-dependent canonical transformation of the coupled macrospin Hamiltonian and validate it with zero-temperature and finite-temperature atomistic spin-dynamics simulations.
result: They identify a threshold-free intrinsic phase-locking mechanism arising from easy-plane anisotropy and strong antiferromagnetic exchange, yielding robust relative-phase stability, bounded thermal fluctuations, and milliradian-scale phase noise.
conclusion: Mn2Au is supported as a highly coherent platform for continuous-wave terahertz generation, and the work provides design principles for stable antiferromagnetic oscillators.

title: Electrical Manipulation Of Centrosymmetric Antiferromagnets By Néel Torque
authors: Jin Cao, Weikang Wu, Huiying Liu, Shen Lai, Cong Xiao, Qian Niu, X C Xie And Shengyuan A Yang
abstract: Electric control of Néel vector is a central task of antiferromagnetic (AFM) spintronics. The major scheme so far has relied on the Néel spin–orbit torque, which however is restricted to AFMs with broken inversion symmetry. Here, we explore a nonlinear Néel torque, uniquely enabling electric control in the vast class of centrosymmetric AFMs including altermagnets, where the existing scheme fails. This new type of Néel torque operates in both AFM metals and insulators, and can appear in all collinear AFM configurations in all the 122 magnetic point groups. Combined with first-principles calculations, we predict significant effects in centrosymmetric AFMs MnRh, MnBi Te and altermagnet CrSb. Our work offers a new and general strategy for Néel torque, significantly broadens the scope of electric control of AFM systems, and opens a new arena in the field of AFM spintronics.
tldr: The paper proposes a nonlinear Néel torque that enables electrical control of the Néel vector in centrosymmetric antiferromagnets and altermagnets, where conventional Néel spin–orbit torque fails.
motivation: Electric control of the Néel vector is central to antiferromagnetic spintronics, but the existing Néel spin–orbit torque scheme requires broken inversion symmetry, excluding the vast class of centrosymmetric AFMs and altermagnets.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework for a nonlinear Néel torque arising in all collinear AFM configurations across the 122 magnetic point groups, and combine it with first-principles calculations for candidate materials.
result: Significant Néel torque effects are predicted in centrosymmetric AFMs MnRh, MnBi2Te4, and the altermagnet CrSb, operating in both metallic and insulating AFMs.
conclusion: The work offers a general strategy for electrical Néel-vector manipulation, broadening the scope of electric control in AFM systems and opening a new direction in antiferromagnetic spintronics.

title: Two-dimensional Beam Compression For Sub-femtosecond Electron Beam Generation
authors: Weihang Liu, Shimin Jiang, Xiao Li, Xingguang Liu, Yi Jiao And Sheng Wang
abstract: Sub-femtosecond electron beams are powerful probes of ultrafast electronic, atomic, and nuclear dynamics, and promising drivers for ultrashort radiation generation from the extreme-ultraviolet to gamma-ray regimes. However, producing such beams at hundred-MeV energies with pC-level charge remains challenging. Here wedevelop a two-dimensional beam-compression scheme based on transverse–longitudinal coupling, in which dispersive beam optics convert the small transverse emittance of modern electron beams into an ultrashort bunch length. Linear analysis and particle tracking show that, after the dominant longitudinal and energy-spread contributions are cancelled, the compressed bunch length is governed primarily by transverse beam quality and collective-effect growth. We further derive and verify a scaling model that captures collective-effect-induced bunch-length degradation and provides a charge–energy operating map for sub-femtosecond compression. Start-to-end simulations of a realistic injector-to-compressor beamline produce a 200 MeV, pC-level bunch with a bunch length of 0.45 fs and a peak current of about 3.5 kA. Jitter studies over a broad range of beam energies show that the output bunch-length distribution narrows and then varies only weakly with increasing energy. These results suggest a feasible route toward compact, high-energy attosecond electron beam sources and may provide a basis for future sub-femtosecond radiation sources based on undulator emission or inverse Compton scattering.
tldr: A two-dimensional beam-compression scheme using transverse-longitudinal coupling generates sub-femtosecond, pC-level electron beams at 200 MeV for ultrafast probes and radiation sources.
motivation: Sub-femtosecond electron beams are valuable probes of ultrafast dynamics and drivers of ultrashort radiation, but producing them at hundred-MeV energies with pC-level charge remains difficult.
method: The authors use dispersive beam optics to convert transverse emittance into ultrashort bunch length, supported by linear analysis, particle tracking, scaling models for collective effects, and start-to-end simulations of an injector-to-compressor beamline.
result: The scheme yields a 200 MeV, pC-level bunch with 0.45 fs bunch length and about 3.5 kA peak current, with jitter studies showing weakly varying output bunch length at higher energies.
conclusion: This offers a feasible route toward compact high-energy attosecond electron beam sources and may enable future sub-femtosecond radiation sources via undulator emission or inverse Compton scattering.

title: Advances In Laser-assisted Nuclear Decay And Nuclear Excitation
authors: Q Xiao, J H Cheng, Y Y Xu, Y T Zou, Z Z Ren, A Ya Dzyublik And T P Yu
abstract: From the synthesis and evolution of the elements to the celestial nuclear processes of stellar explosions and neutron star mergers, nuclear physics is the foundation of our understanding of the Universe. After more than a century of progress, the field of nuclear physics remains vibrant. The rapid advancement of laser technology has opened unprecedented avenues in nuclear physics, driven by the interdisciplinary convergence of laser physics, nuclear structure, plasma science, and quantum dynamics. This emerging field enables studies on laser-induced nuclear excitation, laser-assisted nuclear decay, and precision manipulation of nuclear isomers for optical clocks. This review comprehensively examines the research achievements over the past decade regarding the influence of lasers on radioactive charged-particle emissions and nuclear excitation. Regarding theoretical developments, the review details various methods used to evaluate the interactions between lasers and nuclei, including the time-dependent Schrödinger equation for decay, proton radioactivity, and two-proton radioactivity and Fermi’s golden rule for nuclear excitation as well as the application and advancement of various theoretical models and approximation methods. In experimental research, the review synthesizes significant breakthroughs in laser-induced nuclear excitation experiments, particularly emphasizing the excitation of the Th, Kr, and Sc. These achievements provide essential groundwork for future breakthroughs in both fundamental nuclear science and its broader technological applications.
tldr: This review surveys theoretical and experimental advances in laser-assisted nuclear decay and laser-induced nuclear excitation over the past decade.
motivation: Nuclear physics is fundamental to understanding the Universe, and rapid laser advances create new opportunities for controlling nuclear processes through interdisciplinary laser-nuclear-plasma-quantum dynamics.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks such as the time-dependent Schrödinger equation for decay and Fermi's golden rule for excitation, along with various models and approximation methods, and synthesizes experimental breakthroughs.
result: It highlights significant experiments on laser-induced nuclear excitation, particularly in Th, Kr, and Sc, and details progress in laser-assisted charged-particle emission and isomer manipulation for optical clocks.
conclusion: These achievements provide essential groundwork for future breakthroughs in fundamental nuclear science and related technological applications.

title: Attosecond Molecular Physics In Large (bio) Molecules: A Perspective On An Unexplored Landscape
authors: V Despré, S Palakkal, E Munaro-Langloÿs And F Lépine
abstract: The 2023 Nobel Prize in Physics recognized attosecond science and technology, which allows us to understand and control the properties of matter by accessing electron dynamics at the Angstrom length scale. Attosecond science and technology are currently being applied to investigate all phases of matter and have garnered particular attention in the field of light-induced processes in molecules. After two decades of development, an attosecond perspective on molecular processes has become a tangible reality thanks to advanced experiments and theories. However, so far, this has only been applied to small model systems. This article discusses the current state of the field and explores how it could expand to include the study of complex structures, including large biomolecules.
tldr: A perspective article surveying attosecond science in molecular physics and arguing for its extension from small model systems to large (bio)molecules.
motivation: Attosecond science has matured over two decades but has so far been restricted to small model molecules, leaving electron dynamics in complex biological systems largely unexplored.
method: The authors review the current state of attosecond molecular physics, including advanced experimental and theoretical techniques, and outline conceptual pathways toward studying larger, more complex structures.
result: The article consolidates the field's achievements in light-induced molecular processes and identifies the technical and theoretical obstacles that currently prevent attosecond methods from being applied to large biomolecules.
conclusion: Expanding attosecond spectroscopy to complex (bio)molecular systems is presented as a promising but currently unattained frontier that would deepen understanding of ultrafast electron dynamics in biologically relevant matter.

title: Frustrated Shapes Of Solid Domains In Fluid Vesicle Membranes: From Rolls And Folds To Crumples And Wrinkles
authors: Geunwoong Jeon, Anthony N A Prempeh, Maria M Santore And Gregory M Grason
abstract: Fluid-solid composite vesicles, comprising 2D solid domains integrated into a topologically closed otherwise fluid lipid bilayer membrane, exhibit complex morphologies arising from the geometric frustration between spherical closure of the membrane and 2D solid elasticity. This scenario is distinct from the better studied case of multi-fluid domain vesicles. Here, we study the elastic energies and shape equilibria of a closed vesicle membrane containing a single, flexible circular solid domain using discrete finite-element (Surface Evolver) simulations, determining the key physical and mechanical parameters to govern shape selection. While we find that the 2D solid (shear) elasticity has minimal impact on the highly-under inflated morphologies, the geometrically non-linear resistance of the 2D solid to Gaussian curvature substantially impacts the shape and elastic patterns form for inflated vesicles, by an amount that it grows with ratio of vesicle size to the elastic thickness of solid. For sufficiently large (thin) vesicles we characterize a generic sequence of ground state patterns of solid shape with increasing inflation: from cylindrical rolls and isometric folds to spatially complex patterns of crumples and wrinkles and ultimately to smooth caps. This sequence of non-isometric patterns at high-inflation is shown to be governed by the same far-from-threshold mechanics used to describe similar shape transitions in microscopic sheets on curved liquid interfaces, establishing that inflated shapes are governed by two basic mechanical scales of membrane tension. We find our predictions for highly-anisotropic shape equilibria of fluid-solid composite vesicles closely match experimentally observed shapes of giant unilamellar vesicles of phase-separated DPPC and DOPC. Our study reveals new connection between multi-component vesicles and the geometrically non-linear mechanics of thin solids, and more broadly suggests new principles for pattern control and selection in this paradigmatic class of biological soft matter.
tldr: This paper studies the shape equilibria of fluid-solid composite vesicles containing a single solid domain, using finite-element simulations to identify how solid elasticity and membrane tension govern morphological transitions from rolls and folds to crumples and wrinkles.
motivation: Understanding the geometric frustration between spherical membrane closure and 2D solid elasticity is important for explaining the morphologies of composite vesicles, which differ from better-studied multi-fluid domain vesicles.
method: The authors employ discrete finite-element (Surface Evolver) simulations to compute elastic energies and determine shape equilibria as a function of physical and mechanical parameters.
result: While 2D shear elasticity has minimal impact on under-inflated shapes, the geometrically nonlinear resistance to Gaussian curvature strongly affects inflated shapes, producing a generic sequence of patterns with increasing inflation: rolls, folds, crumples, wrinkles, and smooth caps.
conclusion: The predicted highly anisotropic shapes closely match experimental observations of phase-separated DPPC/DOPC giant unilamellar vesicles, revealing connections between multi-component vesicles and the geometrically nonlinear mechanics of thin solids.

title: Turbulent Magnetogenesis And Large-scale Magnetic Dynamo Amplification In Ion–electron Plasmas
authors: Fabio Bacchini, Francesco Pucci, Sergio Servidio, Francesco Valentini And William H Matthaeus
abstract: Using fully kinetic simulations that capture unprecedentedly large (from electron to ion) scales, we study magnetogenesis driven by continuous large-scale forcing until nonlinear dynamo saturation. We uncover a two-stage mechanism in collisionless ion–electron plasmas whose dynamics diverge dramatically from the pair-plasma case. In the first phase, electron pressure anisotropy triggers electron-Weibel modes, seeding small-scale magnetic fields. Then, a second growth phase emerges when the more massive ions develop their own strong anisotropy and drive ion-Weibel-type modes; concurrently, a Biermann-battery mechanism contributes to amplifying the magnetic field. This combined dynamics provides a tenfold amplification of the magnetic field in comparison to the pair-plasma case. Over long times, dynamo action continues until the system reaches a statistical steady state. This self-consistent kinetic mechanism provides a plausible explanation for robust magnetogenesis wherever an external forcing continuously stirs the plasma.
tldr: Kinetic simulations reveal a two-stage electron- and ion-Weibel plus Biermann-battery mechanism that amplifies magnetic fields in turbulent ion-electron plasmas, far exceeding pair-plasma results.
motivation: The origin of cosmic magnetic fields remains unclear, and collisionless plasma dynamo amplification from electron to ion scales is poorly understood.
method: Fully kinetic particle-in-cell simulations with unprecedentedly large scale separation capture continuous large-scale forcing until nonlinear dynamo saturation.
result: A two-stage growth occurs: electron pressure anisotropy drives electron-Weibel modes, then ion anisotropy drives ion-Weibel modes while a Biermann battery contributes, yielding tenfold field amplification over pair plasmas.
conclusion: The self-consistent kinetic mechanism offers a plausible robust magnetogenesis pathway wherever external forcing stirs ion-electron plasmas.

title: Singularities And The Divergence Of Spherical Harmonic Expansions: Axially Symmetric Planets
authors: Gerald V Dunne, Ovidiu Costin, Crichton Ogle, Michael Bevis And Robert A Ashcraft
abstract: The region of convergence of the spherical harmonic expansion (SHE) is determined by the (generally complex) singularities of the gravitational potential. This complex analysis perspective is at the heart of recent rigorous results concerning the divergence properties of the SHE. In this paper we build physical intuition for these general mathematical results using illustrative examples (some familiar and some new) of idealized planets for which the analysis is particularly explicit. This approach provides new methods to determine the region of convergence, without computing and analyzing expansion coefficients, and gives a novel geometric understanding of the divergence phenomenon. It also explains the fundamental origin of the numerical instabilities inherent to polyhedral models of planets. For the sake of clarity, we illustrate this new approach for the special case of axisymmetric planets of constant density, with explicit comparisons, but the key ideas do not rely on these restrictions.
tldr: The paper analyzes the convergence and divergence of spherical harmonic expansions for gravitational potentials using complex singularities, with illustrative axisymmetric planet models.
motivation: To build physical intuition for rigorous mathematical results on spherical harmonic expansion divergence and to explain numerical instabilities in polyhedral planet models.
method: Complex analysis of potential singularities applied to explicit constant-density axisymmetric planets, avoiding direct computation of expansion coefficients.
result: Shows that the region of convergence is determined by complex singularities, provides a geometric understanding of divergence, and identifies the origin of numerical instabilities in polyhedral models.
conclusion: Offers new methods to determine convergence regions and a geometric perspective on divergence, with key ideas generalizable beyond the axisymmetric constant-density case.

title: Symmetry-enriched Topological Order In Tensor Networks: Defects, Gauging And Anyon Condensation
authors: Dominic J. Williamson, Nick Bultinck, And Frank Verstraete
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2199 (2026).

We study symmetry-enriched topological order in two-dimensional tensor network states by using graded matrix product operator algebras to represent symmetry-induced domain walls. A close connection to the theory of graded unitary fusion categories is established. Tensor network representations of the topological defect superselection sectors are constructed for all domain walls. The emergent symmetry-enriched topological order is extracted from these representations, including the symmetry action on the underlying anyons. Dual phase transitions, induced by gauging a global symmetry, and condensation of a bosonic subtheory, are analyzed and the relationship between topological orders on either side of the transition is derived. Several examples are worked through explicitly.

title: Piston Control In A Two-ion Quantum Device
authors: E Ya Sherman And Andreas Ruschhaupt Jing Li
abstract: We propose a scheme for piston control in a two-ion quantum device with motion confined to orthogonal axes. In this system, one ion plays the role of a ‘classical’ piston driven by the Coulomb interaction with the other ion, whose quantum motion is controlled through modulation of its trapping potential. The stationary state is determined self-consistently, taking quantum effects into account. We identify a narrow quantum regime of the ground state connecting two broad classical regimes. We further design inverse-engineering protocols to control the motion of the ‘classical’ ion. The proposed control scheme provides a useful route toward controlled piston dynamics in microscopic quantum devices.
